name: vol_regime_adaptive_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Intraday market behavior differs fundamentally across volatility regimes. In low-vol regimes (ATR percentile < 30), mean-reversion dominates because moves are small and revert quickly. In high-vol regimes (ATR percentile > 70), momentum dominates because large moves carry information and attract order flow. In medium-vol (30-70th percentile), both strategies underperform — the strategy goes flat. By bucketing ATR(14) into percentile categories using a 5-day rolling ATR distribution and applying different entry rules per regime, we capture regime-specific alpha. The inefficiency persists because volatility-conditional strategies require continuous regime monitoring and parameter switching that most static trading systems cannot accommodate.
mechanism: Market microstructure varies across volatility regimes. In low-vol regimes, mean-reversion dominates as market makers provide tight liquidity. In high-vol regimes, momentum persists as liquidity thins and stop-cascades amplify moves. Adapting the signal to the current regime captures the appropriate edge for prevailing conditions.

conditions: LOW-VOL: Vol_Regime == LOW AND close < BB_lower AND close < vwap (mean-reversion buy)
HIGH-VOL: Vol_Regime == HIGH AND EMA(close,9) > EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap AND volume > 2 * SMA(volume,20) (momentum buy)
LOW-VOL: Vol_Regime == LOW AND close > BB_upper AND close > vwap (mean-reversion sell)
HIGH-VOL: Vol_Regime == HIGH AND EMA(close,9) < EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap AND volume > 2 * SMA(volume,20) (momentum sell)

exit.signal_exit: Vol_Regime transitions to MED (medium vol) — close position as edge dissipates

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 28; adjust regime thresholds if VIX > 22 (shift ATR percentile buckets up by 10)
filters.volume_filter: HIGH-VOL entries require volume > 2x SMA(volume,20); LOW-VOL has no additional volume filter

weaknesses: Medium-vol regime (30-70th percentile of ATR) accounts for ~40% of the time, during which the strategy is flat — significant opportunity cost and underutilization of capital
Regime transitions from LOW to HIGH can be abrupt (e.g., sudden news) — the 10-bar stability requirement causes the strategy to miss the most profitable initial bars of a vol spike
BB(20, 1.5) in low-vol regime uses narrow bands (1.5 sigma vs standard 2.0) — more signals but also more false signals in low-vol environments where noise dominates
prior_art: Volatility regime-switching in Ang & Chen (2002); ATR-based position sizing (Van Tharp); volatility clustering (Mandelbrot); regime-conditional mean-reversion/momentum widely discussed in quant literature
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
